summary: Get all rate values for a rate table (Project)
description: Retrieves all active rate values for a project-level rate table, grouped by condition. For each condition and rate column combination, if a project-level rate value exists, it is returned; otherwise, the company-level rate value is returned. Optional effective_at resolves values as of that datetime.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the company

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project

parameters.name: rate_table_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the rate table

parameters.name: effective_at
parameters.description: When provided, returns values active at this ISO 8601 datetime (empty if none). When omitted, listing uses now and still shows a future or expired table snapshot.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by condition: for Labor use work_classification (asc) or -work_classification (desc) by name, or work_classification_abbreviation (asc) or -work_classification_abbreviation (desc) by abbreviat...

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search by condition: for Labor, matches work classification name or abbreviation; for Equipment, matches equipment type name or category name. Case-insensitive partial match.

200.description: Retrieves all active rate values for a project-level rate table, grouped by condition. Project-level rate values take precedence over company-level rate values.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.
